# D - Sound Studio research (step 5), 2026-10-10

Labels: VERIFIED (url) = I opened it this session. UNVERIFIED = memory or search snippet only. Page budget used: 12 of 12 (some fetches returned thin summaries, noted).

## 1. Minecraft Java sound system

**sounds.json** (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sounds.json)
- Lives at `assets/<namespace>/sounds.json` in a resource pack. Top level maps an **event key** (e.g. `entity.zombie.hurt`, or a custom `banshee.wail`) to `{ "replace": bool, "subtitle": "<lang key>", "sounds": [...] }`.
- Each `sounds` entry is either a bare string (file path without `.ogg`, optional `namespace:` prefix) or an object: `name`, `type` (`file` default, or `event` to reference another event), `volume` (>0, default 1), `pitch` (>0, default 1), `weight` (int, random pick bias), `stream` (true for long sounds; wiki recommends it for music/records), `attenuation_distance` (int), `preload` (bool).
- Event vs file: the game plays an **event key**; the engine picks one entry from the list by weight (variants). Files are the raw Ogg Vorbis. Variants are how you avoid repetition (author 3-4 per hurt/step).
- `replace: true` discards the vanilla list for that event; false/absent appends to vanilla variants.
- Format: **Ogg Vorbis required**. **Mono = positional** (volume falls with distance); **stereo = constant volume** regardless of distance. So every mob/world sound must be mono; only music/UI may be stereo. All VERIFIED same URL.
- Custom namespaces: use `namespace:key` / `namespace:path` (VERIFIED same URL). Put a plugin's keys in its own namespace (e.g. `nxeon_banshee:`), never `minecraft:`.
- Subtitles: `subtitle` is a translation key; the text must exist in `assets/<ns>/lang/en_us.json` (UNVERIFIED detail, standard behaviour).

**What a pack can override vs add** (reasoning; UNVERIFIED in game by me)
- Override `entity.<mob>.hurt/death/ambient/step`: changes that sound for EVERY vanilla mob of that type server-wide, for each player with the pack. Fine for a total-conversion, bad for a mod that adds one "banshee" built on a zombie.
- Add new keys (`ns:banshee.wail`): triggered only by plugin code. This is the right default for Cyrus: new keys, plugin plays them, and silences the vanilla base mob (`Entity#setSilent(true)`, UNVERIFIED API name) so vanilla zombie groans do not overlap.
- Plugin playback (Paper/Bukkit): `World#playSound(Location, String key, SoundCategory, volume, pitch)` and `Player#playSound(...)` take a **string key**, so custom keys work without an enum (UNVERIFIED signatures; check against the Paper jar's javap during build sheets). Category (`HOSTILE`, `NEUTRAL`, `PLAYERS`, `AMBIENT`, `MASTER`...) controls the client's per-category volume slider. Volume above 1.0 extends audible range (rule of thumb ~16 blocks x volume; UNVERIFIED).
- If the player lacks the pack, an unknown key plays silently, so a mod must degrade gracefully.

**Versions**: wiki's sounds.json page has no 1.21.x/26.x entries (VERIFIED same URL), i.e. the schema looks stable since 1.13 (`preload`). 26.1 is the first year-based release; resource pack format is now **84.0** (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_26.1), which matches G-gaps: pack.ts tables are wrong for 26.x. 26.1 also added baby-mob and adult-variant sounds (same URL), so vanilla event names have grown; do not hard-code a list, read keys from the version's asset index. Pack metadata (`pack.mcmeta`, min/max format) is a pack-builder concern, not a sounds.json one. 1.21.11 -> 26.x pack_format deltas for sounds: none found.

**Complete mob sound set** (durations/levels are conventions, UNVERIFIED; tune against vanilla files by measuring them with ffprobe/ebur128 during MVP):

| event | purpose | variants | length | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ambient/idle | random loop-free grunt | 3 | 0.8-2.5 s | quietest, low pitch jitter |
| hurt | damage taken | 3 | 0.2-0.6 s | sharp transient |
| death | on death | 1-2 | 0.6-1.8 s | longest decay |
| step | per footstep | 4 | 0.08-0.25 s | very short, no tail |
| attack | melee swing/bite | 2-3 | 0.3-0.8 s | loud transient |
| special | ability/charge/roar/boss phase | 1-2 each | 0.5-3 s | one key per ability |
| spawn | summon/appear | 1 | 0.8-2.5 s | optional |

Loudness: peak-normalise to about -3 dBFS, attack/death loudest, step/ambient 6-10 dB lower; use `volume` in sounds.json for relative balance rather than re-baking (UNVERIFIED convention). Mono, 44.1 kHz, trimmed with 5 ms fades to avoid clicks. Keep files small (pack size matters for the join prompt).

## 2. Ogg Vorbis pipeline

- **Server-side ffmpeg + libvorbis (recommended).** FFmpeg is LGPL 2.1 by default and becomes GPL 2 if GPL parts are enabled (`--enable-gpl`) (VERIFIED https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html). That page does NOT address libvorbis or the separate-process case (it said so). libvorbis/libogg are BSD-3 (VERIFIED https://github.com/erikh2000/sl-web-ogg, bundled Xiph COPYING files). Calling ffmpeg as a subprocess on a service we run, never redistributing the binary, is the low-risk pattern; legal sign-off still advisable (UNVERIFIED legal reading). Distro ffmpeg is often built with GPL flags; use the distro package unmodified on the server (no redistribution) or a static LGPL build.
- Command shape: `ffmpeg -nostdin -i in.wav -ac 1 -ar 44100 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 out.ogg` (UNVERIFIED flags; the native `vorbis` encoder is experimental, prefer libvorbis).
- **Safe use on the build host**: spawn with an argv array (no shell), `-protocol_whitelist file` and file inputs only (no URLs), CPU/time/memory limits (`timeout`, cgroup), max input size and duration (e.g. 60 s), run in the existing build container, never feed user-supplied filter strings. ffmpeg decoders have a CVE history, so keep it patched and sandboxed.
- `oggenc` (vorbis-tools) is GPL-2 (UNVERIFIED); fine as a separate process but ffmpeg already covers it and decodes MP3, so skip it.
- **Browser/wasm**: `sl-web-ogg` MIT + BSD-3 Xiph parts, `encodeAudioBuffer()` with quality param, promise API, only 17 commits and 0 stars (VERIFIED https://github.com/erikh2000/sl-web-ogg) - immature, treat as a fallback. `libvorbis.js` (itsjoesullivan) BSD-style but old (UNVERIFIED, search snippet). `@wasm-audio-decoders/ogg-vorbis` is decode only (snippet). Browser audio element can already decode Vorbis for preview.
- **Recommendation**: the browser works in WAV/Float32 (`AudioBuffer`) and uploads WAV (or a small JSON edit recipe); the server renders and encodes. This keeps one deterministic encoder, one licence story and lets AI/automatic sound design (no browser) use the same path. Effort S-M.

## 3. Editing UI libraries

| lib | licence | fit |
|---|---|---|
| wavesurfer.js | BSD-3-Clause; v8; plugins Regions, Timeline, Minimap, Envelope, Spectrogram (VERIFIED https://github.com/katspaugh/wavesurfer.js) | waveform display + trim regions + fade envelope UI. Its own docs say it does not process audio. Use as the **view**. |
| Tone.js | MIT, active, `Tone.Offline`, Reverb, Filter, FeedbackDelay, Distortion, pitch shifting (VERIFIED https://github.com/Tonejs/Tone.js) | good for offline rendering of a graph in the browser; heavy (~hundreds KB); optional. |
| howler.js | MIT, 25k stars, playback only (VERIFIED https://github.com/goldfire/howler.js) | not needed; Web Audio suffices. |
| Web Audio (`OfflineAudioContext`) | browser standard | gain, fade (gain ramps), `playbackRate` pitch+speed, `BiquadFilter`, `Convolver` reverb, `DynamicsCompressor`; enough for MVP with no library. |
| audiobuffer-to-wav, jsfx | UNVERIFIED (small MIT-ish utilities) | WAV writer is ~40 lines; write our own. |

Pitch without speed change needs a phase vocoder; skip in MVP (resample pitch only, which is what Minecraft's own `pitch` does).

**Non-destructive recipe** (stored as JSON, source files immutable):
```
{ sourceId, trim:{start,end}, fadeIn, fadeOut, gainDb, pitchSemitones,
  eq:[{type,freq,gain,q}], reverb:{irId,mix}, normalizePeakDb }
```
Layers each carry a recipe, a start offset and a gain; render = sum, then limiter, then mono downmix, then Vorbis. The browser previews via `OfflineAudioContext`; the server re-renders the same recipe for the shipped file. Caveat: browser and server renders must match, so the server is authoritative and the UI preview is approximate. Keep recipe version numbers.

## 4. Automatic sound design

**(a) Procedural synthesis presets** (extend `lib/cyrus/sfx.ts`, which today is UI-only per G-gaps): per sound class a deterministic generator seeded from the spec: growl (saw + formant filters + noise), wail (FM sine glide + vibrato + reverb), hit (noise burst + low sine thump), step (filtered noise click), zap, magic chime. Cheap, free, original, no provenance risk, but sounds synthetic. Effort M. Run it in Node via an offline renderer (the code uses Web Audio; port to a pure-DSP render function; UNVERIFIED how sfx.ts is structured).

**(b) Layering from the owner's 514 SFX library**: filename-prefix tags (Whoosh/Hit/Explosion/Door/Alert...) become a tag index; the LLM picks 1-3 layers per event by tag plus pitch/gain/filters (e.g. low-pass + -7 semitones on an Explosion for a death boom). Pitch-shifting, layering and filtering turns 514 into thousands of distinct sounds. It is the best quality/cost path. Needs the library on the build host, a tag index (can be generated from filenames), and the owner's customer licence. Layer-per-event limit and a "no raw unchanged file" rule are optional policy. Effort M.

**(c) AI generation**:
- Stable Audio Open 1.0: open weights, up to 47 s stereo 44.1 kHz, trained on Freesound CC0/CC-BY/CC-Sampling+ and FMA, "better for sound effects than music", needs a CUDA GPU (VERIFIED https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0). Licence: Stability Community License - free commercial use under USD 1M annual revenue, **registration required**, no using outputs to train foundation models, "Powered by Stability AI" attribution where distributed (VERIFIED https://stability.ai/community-license-agreement). Needs a GPU box Nxeon may not have; no cost per call otherwise. Risky for attribution and registration.
- ElevenLabs Sound Effects API: 0.1-30 s, loopable, MP3 or 48 kHz WAV (non-looping), 40 credits/s when duration specified (VERIFIED https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/sound-effects). Commercial use only on paid plans, no competing-product use (UNVERIFIED, from third-party search snippets; read the actual terms before use). Hosted, sub-minute latency (UNVERIFIED), per-second cost, and it adds a third-party dependency (brand rule: never name it to customers).
- AudioLDM-class (AudioLDM2 weights are non-commercial CC BY-NC as I recall, UNVERIFIED) - avoid unless checked. Not opened due to the page cap; AudioGen/AudioCraft are CC-BY-NC for weights (UNVERIFIED), also avoid.
- Judgment: AI output is useful for textures-of-sound (creature vocals, ambient beds) where layering the owner library falls short; make it a **later** add-on behind a provider interface, every output entering the ledger.

## 5. SoundSpec proposal

```
SoundSpec { version, profile:"minecraft-java", namespace,
  events:[{ key:"banshee.wail", category:"hostile",
     role:"ambient"|"hurt"|"death"|"step"|"attack"|"special"|"spawn",
     variants:[{ weight, volume, pitch, layers:[Layer], mono:true, lengthMs, tailMs }],
     subtitle, stream:false, attenuationDistance }] }
Layer { source:{kind:"library"|"synth"|"ai"|"upload", id|preset|prompt|provenanceId},
        offsetMs, gainDb, recipe:EditRecipe }
```
The compiler turns this into `sounds.json` + Ogg files + lang subtitles + a plugin event table (`role`->key), so Java code never contains file paths. LLM output is schema-validated (event count, length, tag ids must exist, no 'minecraft:' keys unless override is chosen).

**Provenance/licence ledger** (row per layer per render): `{ assetId, kind, licence ("owner-original"|"cc0"|"cc-by"|"generated-<provider>"|"user-upload"), sourceRef (library filename+hash / model+version+prompt hash / upload hash), attributionRequired, commercialOk, customerLicenceVersion, recipeHash, outputHash, userId, createdAt }`. Gate: NxLabs publication refuses public pages when any layer is user-upload without attestation or `attributionRequired` unmet (hook into `public-gate.ts`, per G-gaps). Owner library rows are marked with the licence version once the owner writes it.

## 6. MVP vs later (S <= 2 days, M ~ 1 wk, L multi-week)

MVP: SoundSpec + compiler (sounds.json, lang, ffmpeg encode, pack integration) M; library tag index + LLM layer picking + render service (server DSP: trim/fade/gain/pitch/lowpass/layer) M-L; gate/ledger table S-M; Studio UI with wavesurfer.js (Regions/Envelope) + OfflineAudioContext preview + variant list M; plugin glue (`playSound` helper, silence base mob) S. Later: synthesis presets M, reverb IRs S, pitch-preserving stretch M, AI provider interface L, community sound sharing L.
Build: SoundSpec, compiler, recipe renderer, ledger. Adopt: ffmpeg/libvorbis, wavesurfer.js, Web Audio. Avoid: howler (not needed), NC-licensed models, sl-web-ogg as primary encoder.

Risks: GPL ffmpeg build if redistributed; browser/server render mismatch; customer ownership terms for the owner's library not yet written; vanilla event names change per version.
Could not determine: mob sound lengths from real vanilla files, exact Paper `playSound` overloads on 26.x, ElevenLabs/Stability output terms beyond snippets, quality of any AI model by listening.
### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".

### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.

content.content:
### R1 Assets (about 5 days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Texture slice: spec -> renderer -> validated pack; Style DNA; library of vanilla-style presets + uploads; hybrid JAR + pack install/uninstall (T) | Custom item shows its texture in a real client |
| 6 | Sound slice: tag library, synth presets, server-side mono Ogg, `sounds.json`, subtitles, multi-event per item/mob (T) | Right sounds play per event in a real client; Katara/free correctly blocked |
| 7 | Static 3D item models (the Glock) with display transforms, sounds, particles; vanilla-mob reskin + full sound set (banshee on 1.21.x) (T) | Glock and a banshee skin + sounds install and play |
| 8 | Studios v1: open a mod's assets, edit, re-push pack, revisions, library browsing, quality rubric + gallery (T) | Customer edits a texture/sound and sees it on the server; owner approves the gallery |
| 9 | Hardening: access test matrix, cost estimates per asset op, asset cost caps (2 critique rounds), caching by spec hash | Asset ops priced by measured work; no free bypass |

### R1b Full Texture and Sound Studios (owner priority, added 2026-10-10; Opus for the editor cores)
Moved forward from R3: the studios are a top priority, so the full editors come right after the first asset slice and before composition.
- **Texture Studio (top plan):** full pixel editor (layers, undo/redo, palettes and ramps, selection, tiling and 3D item preview, onion-skin for animated textures), library browsing and search, Style DNA applied across a whole mod, AI edits as non-destructive candidates with before/after diffs, reference-image-to-spec through a vision model, asset history, the quality rubric as a real review screen.
- **Sound Studio (Saka and up):** full waveform editor (zoom, regions, trim, fade, gain, pitch/time, layering, spectrum, loudness and true-peak readouts), library browsing and search by tag, synthesis presets, per-event mob/item sound sets, subtitle keys, non-destructive edit recipes, server-side Ogg export, asset history with waveform diffs.
- **Both:** shared studio core with per-game profiles (Minecraft pixel profile first); plan-tier gates enforced server-side; library follows the studio gate.
- **Done when:** a customer builds a complete set (e.g. banshee skin plus attack/hurt/death sounds) entirely in the studios without touching a prompt, and a real client shows and plays it (T).
- R3 keeps only animated creatures, gameplay designers and playtest scripts.

### R2 Composition, data packs, import (about 7 days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 10-11 | Static conflict engine on the inventory; severity report; reserved-namespace behaviour; mutation corpus (take a good mod, collide IDs) | Seeded conflicts caught with the right class and severity |
| 12 | Mod Pack Builder: manifest, merge (Weld/Beet evaluation), combined boot + differential boots, install/rollback as one unit | Two conflicting mods are caught, resolved or blocked; pack installs and rolls back as a unit |
| 13-14 | Datapack MVP: typed emitters per version, mcdoc validation, boot + RCON check | Valid datapack loads on every listed version |
## Cyrus asset slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (from `feature/cyrus-r0`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.2-4.7 and R1 day 5 (textures); GAPS findings 5, 10, 15 and section D (Style DNA, quality bar). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** No real model build ran: the build service was exercised only through the fake-CLI pipeline test. Sounds are designed to plug into the same path next (see "Sound slice interface").

**The flow.** Build request -> server-side plan gate -> the build service's AI writes texture SPEC files (the existing DSL, Read/Write/Edit only) -> the service validates/renders/quality-checks them like code (bounded repairs) and returns them with the jar -> the portal re-validates, renders the deterministic pack through the version registry, hosts it, computes the Pack Loader entry and records a revision -> (flag-gated) the worker installs the Pack Loader and writes `packs.json` after the jar install.

### 1. Build request (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{kinds,plan,request}.ts`)
- What is REQUESTED: `body.assets` (`["texture"]` or `{ texture: true }`, a request only, never a permission), asset words the Minecraft adapter's route rules recognise in the prompt / change request (`item_model` -> texture, `custom_sound` -> sound), and kinds the base build already has (a change keeps working on them). Passed through `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` and `POST /api/cyrus/generate`.
- What is ALLOWED (`planBuildAssets`, pure): the R0 gate `canAsset(plan, kind, create|edit)` with the plan from the real lookup `tierOf(userId)` (CyrusPlan + admin override; a lookup error = unknown = fail closed), then the version (`itemModelDefinitions`, 1.21.4+; 1.21.1 is refused with "Custom textures need Minecraft 1.21.4 or newer ... Pick 1.21.4 or newer"), then `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY` (`texture: true, sound: false`). Owner rule: free/Katara no assets, Saka sound only, `all` (= Yakko) sound + texture. Only creating/editing is gated.
- Anything refused is a DOWNGRADE: the plugin is built anyway and one customer-visible notice per kind is stored in `ModBuild.cyrus.assets` (`requested`, `allowed`, `notices`, `projectId`, `namespace`; read by `readCyrusMeta`) and returned as `assetNotices` by the builds API. A change to a mod that has textures, on a plan that cannot edit them, says the textures are kept unchanged.
- For an allowed kind the chain's `CyrusProject` is loaded or created (`rootBuildId` = the chain root), so the build has its reserved `nx_<8>` namespace; a project that cannot be created fails closed (no assets, notice).
- **Byte-identical rule**: nothing requested -> no lookups, no project, no `assets` field; requested but refused -> still no `assets` field. Only an allowed request adds `assets: { texture, sound, namespace }` to the service call.

### 2. Build service (`services/modbuilder/{textures.js,prompts.js,server.js,texture-example.json}`)
- `POST /builds` takes `assets` (`textures.js parseAssetsRequest`): unknown fields, non-boolean flags or a namespace that is not `nx_<8>` are a 400; textures on a version without `itemModelDefinitions` in the service's copy of the registry are switched off (defence in depth; an unreadable registry = no textures anywhere). `/health` lists `features.assets: ["texture"]`. Asset builds are never deduped.
- Prompt: the system prompt gets the `CUSTOM TEXTURES` section only when textures are allowed (otherwise it is byte-identical to before; `PROMPT_VERSION` unchanged, texture builds record `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`). It covers the DSL (sizes, palette, all ops), Style DNA (transparent background, 3-5 shade ramps lit from the top-left, flat areas, no noise or gradients, one dark outline colour for the whole mod, diagonal tools like vanilla), the checks it will be held to, "original art only", and the reference rule `meta.setItemModel(new NamespacedKey("<namespace>", "<texture name>"))` (no `setCustomModelData`, never send packs from the plugin). The namespace goes in the user turn (`assetsBlock`), so the section caches per version. Example spec: `texture-example.json` (= the golden ruby sword).
- Workspace allow-list: `assets/textures/<name>.json` survive only when textures are allowed. A change build without texture rights KEEPS the base's specs byte for byte (snapshot; edits are reverted, new files removed): keeping is never gated. The model keeps Read/Write/Edit only; `scan.js` is unchanged (specs are data, not code).
- Each round, after `validate()`: `checkWorkspaceTextures` (JS port of `checkSpec` + renderer + quality bar). HARD problems (invalid JSON/spec, file name != `name`, quality fail, more than 24) go back to the model as `repair-asset` feedback; SOFT ones (reserved namespace literal missing from the Java, a texture no string literal references, a foreign `nx_` namespace) once. Bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` (default 2) and the overall `MB_MAX_REPAIRS`; afterwards a still-failing spec is DROPPED (file deleted, `assetDowngrades`, a warning and a "Good to know" limitation), never shipped.
- `finish()` adds `assetResult: { namespace, promptVersion, qualityVersion, kept, textures: [{ name, path, sha256 (canonical JSON), spec, quality }], downgraded, warnings }`. Specs are part of the persisted source (`files`, `source.zip`).
- Image: `textures.js` and `texture-example.json` must be in the next image, and the registry mounted at `MB_REGISTRY` or `/opt/mb/app/registry.json` (it already is for the JDK map).

### 3. Quality bar v1 (`lib/cyrus/textures/quality.ts` == `textures.js textureQuality`, version `tq-1`)
Runs on the rendered pixels of every texture (service and portal):

| Check | Pass | Warn | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparency | only alpha 0/255, coverage 0.10-0.85 | coverage < 0.10 or > 0.85 | any semi-transparent pixel, coverage < 0.04, or every pixel solid |
| palette_size (distinct colours) | <= 32 / 48 / 64 at 16 / 32 / 64 px | above that | > 48 / 96 / 128 |
| contrast (WCAG ratio darkest vs lightest) | >= 2.5 | 1.6-2.5 | < 1.6 |
| noise (grain: neighbour pairs differing by 1-24 RGB) | <= 0.20 | 0.20-0.35 | > 0.35 |
| outline (dark silhouette pixels) | >= 50 % | below (Style DNA hint only) | never |
| vanilla_lookalike | | | `not_run` stub: needs the vanilla texture set on the build host (GAPS 15) |

Calibrated on the existing reference specs: ruby sword and health potion pass; the Glock (49 colours at 32 px) and the frost blades (noise) warn. Golden fixtures: `test/fixtures/cyrus-textures/` (`ruby_sword` pass, `flat_square` / `tiny_dot` / `noisy_orb` fail), plus a pinned render hash. The report is stored with every asset. The vision-model judge and owner gallery are later (R1 day 8).

### 4. Portal sync (`lib/cyrus/assets/{textures,sync,sync-deps}.ts`, hook in `lib/modbuilder/store.ts`)

Accept the pack to see them.", `required: false`), one `CyrusRevision` (kind `generated`, status `passed`, manifest `plugin/<jar>` artifact + `assets/textures/<name>.json` asset (sha256 of canonical JSON) + `resourcepack/<sha1>.zip` resourcePack, engine record with the asset prompt version and toolchain) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` per texture (mime `application/vnd.nxeon.texture-spec+json`, provenance = spec, quality report, PNG sha256, pack sha1, build id). - Soft cross-checks (namespace literal / unreferenced texture) get one repair and then become warnings, because a plugin may build keys from parts; hard failures are dropped.

This is a key licensing issue — this is a third-party asset bundle with a non-transferable license that explicitly prohibits redistributing the files individually, as a bundle, or uploading them anywhere accessible for others to download or extract. Since resource packs ship as zip files containing raw Ogg audio, distributing one effectively lets players extract and redistribute those licensed sound files, which would violate the terms.

Beyond that, there's a deeper question of whether Nxeon's customers (server owners building mods) are even permitted to use these assets at all, since the license was granted to Nxeon specifically and is non-transferable — this seems like a question for the asset owner to resolve, not something I should assume an answer to. I need to log this clearly in the ledger as an unverified licensing concern rather than asserting originality, noting the exact license document found and its restrictive terms.

Since the real run stays local on node-2 and nothing ships to customers yet, keeping library layers enabled for rendering is safe. I want a policy gate though: unless an explicit clearance flag is set, events using library layers shouldn't ship in production, and I should add a validator rule requiring every library-layer variant to include at least one real transformation (pitch shift, extra layer, or filtering) rather than passing through an unprocessed file.

The licence PDF itself isn't audio, so I can just commit a summary of it in the docs rather than the file. Now I should move on to checking node-2's actual state — SSH access, whether ffmpeg and node are installed, and how the TestFlight SSH invoker is wired up so I can find the right library path.

I should avoid verbose process listings going forward. Since node-2 is a live production host with customer VMs and no ffmpeg installed, I need to set up an isolated ffmpeg under /tank/nxeon-build/tmp — one option is downloading the Debian ffmpeg package and its dependencies with apt-get, then extracting them with dpkg -x, keeping in mind Debian's build includes GPL-licensed components.

Extracting all the libavcodec dependencies that way is cumbersome, so instead I'm leaning toward a static build: either johnvansickle.com's GPLv3 static builds, or BtbN's FFmpeg-Builds on GitHub which offer both GPL and LGPL variants with checksums for verification. I'll grab the LGPL build from BtbN's GitHub releases and verify it against the accompanying checksums.sha256, assuming node-2 has internet access, while also considering whether the libvorbis encoder's output is deterministic given the ogg muxer's use of a random stream serial number.

With `-fflags +bitexact` set on both audio and container flags, ffmpeg should produce byte-identical output across runs on the same build, since bitexact mode fixes the serial number and strips the encoder version metadata tag. For decoding, I plan to have ffmpeg decode the MP3 to floating-point PCM at the original sample rate and channel count, then handle mono downmixing and resampling myself in the DSP chain rather than relying on ffmpeg, since JS double-precision math should be deterministic on a given platform.

Now I'm thinking about where the render actually executes — the instructions say rendering must happen on node-2 via an injectable render-host transport rather than on the primary, meaning the portal would send the SoundSpec JSON to node-2 and get back the encoded Ogg files plus measurements. That implies I need a self-contained render-host runner script on node-2 that takes the spec, library path, and ffmpeg path, performs decode→DSP→encode, and returns JSON with a base64-encoded Ogg plus a PCM hash for verifying determinism — though since the DSP itself is meant to be TypeScript in lib/cyrus/sound/, I need to figure out whether node-2's Node version can run TS directly via type stripping.

Since the repo uses extensionless imports, Node's native type-stripping (which requires full file extensions in import paths) probably won't work cleanly, so I'm considering whether to bundle the TS with esbuild at build time instead of runtime, though that adds complexity. Another option is duplicating the DSP logic as a plain CommonJS JS module alongside the TS version, similar to how textures.js mirrors a TS counterpart elsewhere in the codebase, even though that duplication feels wasteful.

I'll have a build script generate that bundle with esbuild, plus a test verifying the committed bundle stays in sync with its sources via a hash or rebuild comparison.

I should check whether esbuild is actually available in node_modules within the worktree. I'm also weighing whether DSP could run on the portal side instead, but the explicit instruction to keep audio rendering off the primary means everything—including library audio paths on node-2—needs to stay on that remote host.

Library files should be referenced by id through a manifest that maps to filename and sha256, letting the runner verify integrity before decoding. Synth presets can be pure TypeScript bundled into the runner, with golden PCM-hash tests running locally since they're pure computation—though I need to check what devhost actually executes, since it likely also proxies to node-2 for heavier build/agent tasks.

content.content:
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

content.thinking:
I'm planning the sound library module structure: a library file with filename-to-tag parsing, manifest loading, search functions, and a compact catalog format, plus a generated manifest JSON and supporting scripts.

For generating the manifest, I need to decide where to run the build since the scan data lives on node-2's filesystem—devhost mirrors the worktree, so I'll run the TS generator there using tsx, pointing it at the existing scan.json, then pull the resulting manifest back into the primary worktree.

I'm now sketching the DSP module layout: wav.ts for PCM types and WAV encode/decode plus hashing, dsp.ts for pure audio operations like trim, fade, gain, resample, mixing, filtering, echo, reverb, and limiting, and measure.ts for peak/true-peak detection and loudness estimation using K-weighting filters.

I'm also planning synth.ts with a seeded PRNG and sound presets (growl, wail, whoosh, impact, gunshot, UI sounds, magic), spec.ts for the SoundSpec v1 types and validator with a JS twin and equivalence tests against fixtures, and render.ts for a pure function that renders a sound spec from loaded source PCM.

Now I'm outlining quality.ts for sound quality checks like true-peak, loudness bands, silence ratio, DC offset, and duration limits, ffmpeg.ts for decoding/encoding/probing via spawned ffmpeg processes, and runner.ts as the node-2 entry point that reads a job spec from stdin and renders accordingly.

The runner outputs JSON with per-sound variant data including base64-encoded ogg, hashes, measurements, and duration, plus ffmpeg tool version info. I'm also planning a committed esbuild bundle of the runner with a test that rebuilds and compares it for determinism, and a host.ts module defining a RenderHost interface with an SSH-based implementation that pushes the bundle and job over stdin before invoking the renderer remotely.

For testing, I need a fake render host that runs the pure rendering logic in-process with a stub encoder returning deterministic fake ogg bytes, since running the real renderer in-process is off-limits in production but fine on the dev host. There's also host selection logic driven by an environment variable, defaulting to an "unrendered" status when no render host is configured.

Now I'm thinking about how to extend the pack composition logic to support sound assets alongside textures, allowing packs with zero textures when sounds are present.

For sound-only packs I need subtitle entries in the language file and should skip the item-models requirement when there are no textures, plus adjust the resource pack format accordingly. I'm also planning validation logic for sounds to re-check specs and catalog IDs, and extending the sync flow to validate, render via the host, run quality checks, and build packs incorporating both textures and sounds with appropriate status fields. I'm also noting the sounds.json structure, where event keys are namespace-free within the per-namespace file but referenced with the namespace prefix when played.

Working through the file-naming convention for sound specs, I'm reasoning that a single spec file likely represents one sound set (like a creature) containing multiple events such as attack, hurt, and death, each with their own variants, with keys formed as namespace plus set name plus event.

To keep things bounded, I'm setting cost guards: a max of 8 sets per build, 8 events per set, 24 events total, 1-4 variants per event, and up to 4 audio layers per variant.

I'm also capping per-variant duration based on role — step ≤0.5s, hurt ≤1.5s, attack ≤2s, death ≤4s, ambient ≤4s, ability ≤6s, fire ≤2s, reload ≤3s, spawn ≤4s, ui ≤1.5s — plus a total rendered-seconds cap per build. Event names will be free-form slugs paired with a role enum covering ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, fire, and similar categories.

I'm deciding how to structure each sound layer: a source that's either a library reference, a synth preset with params/seed, or silence, plus timing fields like start offset, gain in dB, and pitch expressed in semitones (converted to playback rate via 2^(st/12)), along with trim and fade in/out settings for library sources.

Processing options per variant should cover normalize, lowpass/highpass filters, reverb mix, echo parameters, and fade out. Then I need to define variant, event, and spec-level schemas with their constraints like weight, layer counts, subtitle requirements, and category limits. I also want a rule that rejects any variant that's just a raw unprocessed library sound, forcing some transformation to be applied.

I'll implement this as a validator requiring pitch shift, an additional layer, or some filter/effect whenever a library sound is used, since it's a licensing safeguard against distributing standalone files even though it's not explicitly required by the plan. The validator will need access to a catalog of valid library ids and durations, sourced from a JSON file for the JS service and from the manifest for TS, with equivalence fixtures testing unknown ids too. There's also a licensing gate controlled by an environment variable that determines whether library layers are permitted at all.

Rather than letting the service silently drop library layers when the licence isn't cleared, I think it's better for the portal itself to decide upfront whether the sound library is offered, which means extending the request schema to include a `soundLibrary` flag — though that adds surface area. I'll keep the licence decision purely on the portal side with a policy function checking an environment variable for cleared status.

This flows into two SOUND_SECTION prompt variants (library-enabled vs synth-only), with the JS validator and portal both rejecting library layers when the flag is off — default off until the owner clears it, while real testing on node-2 can still use the library since it's not a customer distribution. Now I need to figure out the render host transport for the actual production path.

If the primary portal needs to render via ssh to node-2, that requires ssh keys from the nxeon app user, which is an owner decision, since the build service VM has no ffmpeg available. Leaving CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST unset means sounds stay as unrendered specs with a notice that rendering isn't switched on yet, and since sync happens at request-time through API polling, the ssh rendering delay across multiple events and variants needs a cap for now, with a note that this should eventually move to a background worker.

For caching, I should key render results by spec hash, library manifest version, and renderer version, so identical inputs always produce the same deterministic output and sync stays idempotent since the pack is content-addressed. For quality failures, I'll drop just the failing variant rather than the whole event unless no variants remain, and the normalization chain should apply DC-blocking via a highpass filter before loudness normalization to catch most silence/duration/DC issues.

I'm defining target loudness bands per sound role (attack/death around -11 LUFS, hurt around -13, ambient around -20, steps around -21, UI around -18, spawn/reload around -16), using whole-signal K-weighted measurement for very short clips under 400ms since gating doesn't work well there, reflecting research that ambient/step sounds should sit 6-10 dB quieter than attack/death sounds.

I'm working out peak limiting logic: normalize gain to the target LUFS, then cap true peak at -1.5 dBTP by taking the minimum of the target gain and the gain needed to hit that ceiling, only flagging a "warn" (not a hard fail) if the resulting loudness drops more than 6 dB below the band minimum.

Since Vorbis encoding can overshoot the original PCM's true peak, I'm planning to measure the final result by decoding the Ogg back and checking true peak on the actual decoded audio players will hear, targeting a pre-encode ceiling of around -1.5 dBTP to leave margin for that overshoot.

For determinism, I need to use bitexact ffmpeg flags and strip metadata so identical inputs always produce byte-identical Ogg output, verifying this by encoding twice and comparing. I'm feeding raw PCM via stdin with no dithering for reproducible rounding, then encoding with libvorbis at a fixed quality setting.

For decoding, I'm restricting the protocol whitelist to file-based access for MP3 inputs (resolved by fixed path and verified checksum), outputting float32 PCM while preserving the original channel count from the manifest rather than forcing mono, and relying on swresample's deterministic behavior for any 48kHz to 44.1kHz conversion.

Synthesis runs at 44100Hz, with all downstream math done in JS float64 before final conversion to s16 PCM with proper rounding and clamping — the PCM checksum comes from the s16le bytes, and a separate checksum covers the final Ogg file.

For deployment, I'm planning to push the small runner bundle over SSH only if it's not already present (checking via a test command before writing it), then execute the job by piping it through stdin in a second SSH call — two calls per render is acceptable given the bundle's small size. The output comes back as JSON with base64-encoded Ogg data, capped at 8MB total.

On the library side, source files live in a configurable directory and the runner checks each one's checksum against the manifest before decoding. I notice the sound naming shifted slightly, which seems fine. The catalog size is acceptable token-wise and documented, and I should verify tsc ran cleanly by checking later. Now I'm moving on to writing the pure unit tests for cyrus-sounds.

I want manifest coverage checking all 514 files for unique ids, correct group/tags/category/ledger fields, matching derived ids and tags, no embedded audio data, reasonable file size, and confirming no actual audio files live in the repo. Then I need search API tests for text/tags/duration/group/limit filters, catalog line-count and artifact-freshness checks via esbuild, spec validation fixtures comparing TS and JS implementations across context variants with error-message checks, and DSP golden hash tests pinning synth preset and variant renders while confirming deterministic output across repeated runs.

I'm working through LUFS and true-peak math for a 1kHz sine test signal, accounting for K-weighting gain to verify expected loudness values and intersample peak behavior where sample peaks underestimate true peak by about 3dB, plus silence/DC offset checks. Beyond that I still need quality-check pass/warn/fail scenarios, pack-building tests with fake Ogg buffers verifying sounds.json structure and format compatibility, duplicate-key and non-Ogg rejection, and sync tests with a fake render host confirming sound-only asset rows get recorded correctly in the pack.

I'm also mapping out additional sync edge cases: idempotent reruns producing the same pack hash, render-off behavior still recording revisions without a pack, dropped library sets, bad hashes from fake hosts causing dropped variants, and quality failures also dropping variants. I need a fake render host that bypasses ffmpeg by synthesizing audio directly and wrapping it in a minimal Ogg-like structure for testing, plus coverage for the gate matrix across plans, prompt section visibility rules, and SSH render host parsing of job output including busy-code handling.

For the mod-page tests, I'm planning to extend the existing fake-CLI pipeline test, so I'm checking how that fake CLI writes its files to model the new behavior correctly.

content.thinking:
I found an important bug: the normalized spec isn't idempotently re-validatable, since normalized layers set trimStart:0 and seed:1 for all types, which the validator rejects for non-lib/non-synth cases. I need to fix the validator so it accepts its own normalized output—likely by allowing trimStart when it's 0 or kind is lib, and handling seed similarly, or by having the normalized form omit irrelevant fields entirely.

I also notice null handling issues: normalized `length: null` for lib and processing fields like lowpass/highpass/echo set to null fail the validator's `!== undefined` checks since null isn't undefined. I need to treat null as equivalent to absent for these fields, and I should add an idempotence test that checks checkSoundSpec(normalized) deep-equals normalized across fixtures in both TS and JS.

Separately, the "Explosion 1.MP3" tagging failure stems from a rule requiring tags.length >= 2 plus group/category match, but this file only has one tag after dedup—I should relax the requirement to length >= 1 since category presence already satisfies the "every file is tagged" rule. The library-not-cleared deep-equal issue likely resolves once other dropped entries like banshee are accounted for after these fixes.

Addendum from the owner to your sound-slice task: the 514-file sound library must become a PROPER, searchable asset library, not just filename tags. Extend step 1 (LIBRARY) as follows, keeping everything metadata-only in git (no audio) and keeping the licence ledger as you have it.

TAXONOMY (apply to every file, deterministic from the filename + measured audio, listed in a committed taxonomy file lib/cyrus/sound/taxonomy.json so it is data, not code):
- category (one primary): Weapons (gunshot, gun reload, cocking/bolt, ricochet, melee swing, sword/metal clash, bow/arrow), Creatures & Voices (animals, growl, scream, gasp, laughter, breath, footsteps/wings), Impacts & Destruction (hit, punch, crash, break, thud, explosion), Movement (whoosh, swoosh, swipe, dash, teleport), Environment & Ambience (ambient, water, wind, rain, crowd, room tone), Doors & Mechanisms (door, doorbell, lock, switch, chest), UI & Alerts (alert, ding, click, notification, success, error, horn, whistle), Crowd & Reactions (applause, cheers), plus 'Other' only as a last resort (report how many land there and why).
- useCases (multi-valued, where a mod would use it): weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient, mob_hurt, mob_death, mob_attack, mob_step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanism, ambience_world, weather, explosion. A gunshot is weapon_fire; a reload/cock is weapon_reload; both also carry the broader tag 'weapon'. Define the mapping rules in the taxonomy file (filename keywords and synonyms -> category/useCases), with a synonym table (gunfire=gunshot, swoosh=whoosh, etc.).
- descriptors (derived from measured audio): durationClass (stinger <0.5 s, short <2 s, medium <6 s, long), intensity (soft/medium/loud from loudness+peak), pitchBand (low/mid/high from spectral centroid; you may compute with ffmpeg/your DSP), character where cheaply derivable (sharp transient vs sustained), loopable heuristic (start/end level match; mark as heuristic), channels.
SEARCH: a pure, tested API (lib/cyrus/sound/library-search.ts): free-text query with synonym expansion and simple ranking (exact tag > category > filename words), plus facets/filters (category, useCase, tags, descriptor ranges, duration range, loopable), pagination, and a 'similar to' helper (same category/useCase and close descriptors). Tests: queries like 'gun', 'reload', 'weapon', 'scary', 'footsteps', 'ui click' return sensible results; every file has a category and at least one useCase or an explicit 'unclassified' reason; the report lists category and useCase counts and the unclassified files so the owner can review them.
OUTPUT: also write a human-readable catalog report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/sound-library-catalog.md (counts per category and use case, example files per bucket, the unclassified list, naming patterns you found) so the owner can review the cataloguing. Keep the compact model-facing catalog small (ids, category, useCases, durationClass only).
Keep this within your existing token budget: it should be mostly data-driven rules plus tests, not extra architecture. Mention the result in your final report.

That regex should work fine. Before rerunning tests, I need to address the coordinator's addendum about taxonomy, which affects the manifest and catalog—starting with a taxonomy.json file mapping synonyms like gunfire to gunshot and swoosh to whoosh.

I'm weighing whether to fold my existing "group" concept into this new taxonomy structure entirely, replacing it with category, prefix, useCases, tags, and descriptors fields, but that ripples into tests and the catalog. Still, it seems cleaner than maintaining two overlapping classification systems, so I'm restructuring library.ts to move GROUP_WORDS into taxonomy.json as categories and useCases.

For the measured descriptors, I realize I need spectral centroid and transient sharpness data, so I'm considering using ffmpeg's aspectralstats filter versus writing a pure TS module that decodes PCM and computes centroid via a simple DFT on frames.

Defining character heuristics...

I need a measurement pass on node-2 producing per-file centroid, attack, and transient data, written as `scripts/cyrus/sound-descriptors.ts` running against the mirrored library with ffmpeg, feeding into sound-manifest.ts so audio never leaves node-2. Then library-search.ts handles searchLibrary with synonym expansion, ranked scoring, and facet filters.

For the model-facing catalog, I'll follow the instruction to only expose id, durationClass, and useCases per line grouped by category, relying on filename slugs embedded in the id to carry descriptive cues like "scream" vs "gasp" since full tags aren't included. The report goes to /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/.

Now I'm drafting taxonomy.json, starting with category definitions: weapons covers gunshots, lasers, reloading/racking sounds, ricochets, swords, bows; creatures_voices covers animal sounds (birds, cats, dogs, crickets) plus human vocalizations like screams, gasps, grunts, groans, laughter, sneezes, snores, yawns, and breathing.

Continuing with impacts_destruction (hits, crashes, explosions, glass breaking, rumbles), movement (whooshes, swishes, swipes, dashes, teleports, slices), and starting environment_ambience (ambient tones, water, rain, wind, thunder).

Continuing doors_mechanisms with lock, switch, chest, zipper, camera shutter, and ratcheting sounds, then moving into ui_alerts covering notification tones, beeps, chimes, bells, success/error sounds, and digital glitches, with some overlap into musical stingers and dramatic reveals that might need their own category.

Given the volume of music stingers, drum hits, record scratches, and cartoon effects like sad trombone, I'm weighing whether to force them into "Other" or justify adding a new "Music & Stingers" category despite the coordinator's preference to avoid extra categories—since dumping 70+ files into Other seems worse than a well-justified deviation I can flag in my report.

Now I'm trying to sort trickier edge cases: digital/glitch/static sounds seem to fit "UI & Alerts," but zap/electrified/laser/shimmer/sparkle are messier since they could map to magic, weapons, or impacts, and none of those map cleanly onto the coordinator's fixed category list.

My judgment call is to add two new categories, "Music & Stingers" and "Magic & Energy," since misfiling these sounds would be worse than deviating slightly from the given list. I'll flag this decision clearly in my report, then move on to sorting crowd reaction terms like applause, cheering, and laughter into the "crowd" category, and start working through vehicle-related terms like car, train, helicopter, and horn.

I'm resolving ambiguous cases by establishing a category-priority order (weapons, doors/mechanisms, creatures/voices, impacts, movement, crowd, UI alerts, magic, music, environment) rather than relying on word order within each title, so something like "Car Door" lands under doors/mechanisms rather than environment, and "Air Horn" or "Train Whistle" fall under UI alerts rather than environment since that category ranks higher in my priority list.

I'm reconsidering edge cases like "Dramatic Buildup Whip," where movement would normally win over music by priority, but music should actually take precedence when a title contains stinger-style words like dramatic, reveal, suspense, or drumroll — so I'm carving out a special rule where those keywords bump music ahead of movement and impacts in the ordering.

Now I'm drafting the useCases keyword mappings, grouping terms like gunshot/laser/bow under weapon_fire, racking/reload/cocking under weapon_reload, impact/punch/slice under weapon_impact, swoosh/whip/sword under melee, and growl/monster under mob_ambient.

I'm continuing through mob_hurt (gasp, groan, scream), mob_death (scream, groan, dying), mob_attack (growl, bite, screech), mob_step (footsteps, creak), and starting ability_cast keywords like whoosh, zap, sparkle, teleport.

I'm now mapping out magic sounds (shimmer, chimes, mystery), boss_event cues (braam, rumble, thunder, explosion), ui_notification terms (ding, beep, click, glitch), and pickup_reward words (ding, jingle, celebratory).

I continue sorting block_interaction sounds (glass, wood, crumple, crash, typing, tape), door_mechanism cues (creak, lock, knocking), ambience_world terms (forest, crowd, underwater, wind, rain), and weather/explosion categories, flagging a few ambiguous terms like "machinery" and "braam" as uncertain fits.

Now I'm also planning broader category groupings for weapon and mob sounds, plus a synonym map so queries like "gun," "swoosh," or "scary" expand to related canonical terms such as gunshot, whoosh, or creepy/monster/growl.

I should also canonicalize synonyms on the tag side, so a file tagged "whoosh" also matches "swoosh" queries — applying the same synonym map both ways. For ranking, each query word expands into variants, and I take the best match score across all those expansions when comparing against tags, use cases, categories, and filenames.

Now I'm shifting to the descriptors module, which needs to extract pitch, loudness, and attack features from the audio and classify them against threshold bands defined in the taxonomy — I'm planning to derive those thresholds empirically from the actual loudness distribution across the sound files rather than guessing fixed values.

I'm sketching the pipeline: a script running on node-2 decodes each file via the runner's ffmpeg path, computes raw descriptor numbers, and writes them to a scratch JSON file; a separate manifest script later merges that with the scan results. Sequential decoding across the ~514 files should take a minute or two, which is acceptable within the agent slice.

I'm refining the mappings further — pump/loading to weapon_reload, snap added to ui alert keywords, yawn to mob_ambient, rewind to ability_cast, and sad trombone/rimshot as failure-reaction sounds. For musical cues with no real gameplay tie-in, I need to remember the rule that every file still needs a category plus either a useCase or an explicit "unclassified" justification.

I'll leave music files unclassified with a clear reason since they don't map to gameplay. ## Cyrus sound slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (2026-10-10), on top of the asset slice above. MASTER-PLAN 4.7 (Sound, Saka+) and R1 day 6. **Nothing is deployed or switched on**: sound rendering is OFF unless `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, the owner's library is OFF for customer builds unless `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`, and delivery still needs `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1`. No real model build ran; no client heard anything.

**The flow.** Build request (plan gate: sound = Saka and the top plan) -> the service's AI writes SoundSpec files `assets/sounds/<set>.json` (one SET per mob/item/spell, events inside) -> the service validates them like code (bounded repairs, drop-don't-ship) and returns them in `assetResult.sounds` -> the portal re-validates (library licence policy, budgets) and sends a render job (specs + library refs, NO audio) to the RENDER HOST (node-2) -> node-2 decodes library MP3s, runs the pure DSP chain, encodes mono Ogg Vorbis, decodes it back and runs the quality bar -> the portal checks every returned file (sha256, `OggS`, mono Vorbis, verdict) and adds `sounds.json` + subtitles + the Oggs to the SAME pack as the textures -> hosting, Pack Loader entry, revision and delivery are shared with textures (one pack per mod).

### 1. Library (`lib/cyrus/sound/{{library,library-search,classify,descriptors}}.ts`, `taxonomy.json`, `library.manifest.json`)
- The owner's zip (`board-uploads/.../819080d91d471a0eceeab422.zip`, sha256 `5796b4ac...86c9`, 514 MP3 + 1 PDF) was copied to node-2 and extracted to `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/sound-library/files` (read-only, dir mode 700). **No audio is in git, in /opt/nxeon or in any served directory**; a test fails if an audio file is tracked.
- `library.manifest.json` (metadata only, generated by `scripts/cyrus/sound-manifest.ts` from two scans run ON node-2: `scan.py`-style ffprobe + ebur128/astats, and `scripts/cyrus/sound-descriptors.ts`): per file a stable id `<slug>_<4 hex of the content sha256>`, file name, prefix, category, use cases, tags, descriptors, raw measurements (centroid, attack, front energy, start/end level, crest), duration, sample rate (455 x 44.1 kHz, 59 x 48 kHz), channels (all stereo), bit rate, LUFS, true/sample peak, RMS, DC, sha256, and a **ledger row**: `provenance: owner-provided (2026-10-10)`, `licenceStatus: unverified: owner to document source per file group`. Originality is never asserted.
- **Licence finding**: the zip contains `_Essential Sound Effects Bundle License.pdf` (sha256 `ab1a9796...0db3`) naming Excelerator.tech as licensor: non-transferable, royalty-free, modify + use in games allowed, but it prohibits distributing / making available the files individually or as part of another bundle or package and uploading them where others can access them as standalone files. A resource pack puts (processed) Oggs on every player's client. Hence: customer builds do not get the library until the owner confirms (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`), and the validator refuses a variant that would ship one library sound unchanged (needs pitch, another layer or an effect). Not legal advice.
- **Taxonomy** (data in `taxonomy.json`, applied by `classify.ts`; owner review report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/sound-library-catalog.md`): file-name words -> synonym table (gunfire/gunshots -> gunshot, swoosh/swish -> whoosh, clapping -> applause...) -> category = first category in file order whose keywords hit the prefix words, else any word. Categories: {catline}. `music_stingers` and `magic_energy` were added to the 8 requested so musical cues and magic sounds do not land in `other` (now 0 files). Use cases (multi-valued): weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient/hurt/death/attack/step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanism, ambience_world, weather, explosion; weapon_* / melee also carry the tag `weapon`. {nouse} files (mostly music beds, record scratches, instrument notes) have no use case and carry an explicit `unclassified` reason. Descriptors (thresholds in taxonomy.json): durationClass (stinger < 0.5 s, short < 2 s, medium < 6 s, long), intensity (soft < -24 LUFS, loud >= -16 LUFS or peak >= -1 dBFS at >= -20 LUFS), pitchBand (spectral centroid < 1.5 kHz low, >= 3.5 kHz high), character (transient vs sustained from front energy / attack / crest), loopable (HEURISTIC: start/end level within 4 dB, >= 1 s; 3 files), channels.
- **Search** (`library-search.ts`, pure): free text with synonym expansion (`querySynonyms`: gun -> gunshot/reload/weapon, scary -> creepy/scream/suspense/growl/..., ui -> ui_alerts) and ranking exact tag (5; 4 via a synonym) > use case / category (3) > tag prefix (2) > file-name word (1), every query word must match; filters (category, useCase, tags, durationClass, intensity, pitchBand, character, loopable, duration range), facets, pagination, `similarTo(id)` (same category, shared use cases, close descriptors).
- **Model catalog**: `services/modbuilder/sound-catalog.txt` (generated, ~23 KB): `<id> <durationClass> <useCases>` grouped by category, nothing else; `sound-catalog.json` = id -> seconds for the validator.

### 2. Audio pipeline (`lib/cyrus/sound/{{dsp,measure,render,runner,host,job}}.ts`, `runner.bundle.cjs`)
- **ffmpeg on node-2, isolated**: BtbN FFmpeg-Builds static release `autobuild-2026-10-09-14-16`, file `ffmpeg-n8.1.3-16-ge0a878dd70-linux64-lgpl-8.1.tar.xz`, sha256 `9ee0b516...e5e1` (matched GitHub's asset digest and the release `checksums.sha256`), extracted to `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/ffmpeg/` (`current` -> it). Binaries: ffmpeg `bcb7aa88...30d6`, ffprobe `6e048ec2...86c1`. **Licence: LGPL v3 or later** (`--enable-version3`, no `--enable-gpl`, no nonfree; `ffmpeg -L` says LGPL 3); it includes libvorbis (BSD) and libmp3lame. Only glibc is dynamic. Run as a separate process only, argv arrays, `-protocol_whitelist file` (decode) / `pipe` (encode/probe), never user filter strings; never redistributed.
- **DSP** (pure, Float64, 44.1 kHz mono): downmix, trim, gain, raised-cosine fades, pitch by resampling (cubic Hermite; speed changes with pitch like Minecraft's own `pitch`), mix at offsets, RBJ biquads (low/high/band/shelf), DC block, echo, small Schroeder reverb, silence trim, look-ahead limiter, length cap, s16 conversion, WAV writer. Render chain per variant: layers -> processing -> 30 Hz cut + DC block -> trim silence -> cap at the role's max -> edge fades -> normalise to the role's loudness target -> limiter at -1.5 dBFS. **Measurement**: sample peak, true peak (4x Hann-windowed sinc), integrated loudness (BS.1770 K-weighting, 400 ms blocks, absolute + relative gates; one ungated block for clips < 400 ms), silence ratio (10 ms windows < -50 dBFS), DC offset.
- **Runner on node-2** (`runner.ts`, bundled with esbuild to `runner.bundle.cjs`, committed; a test fails when it is stale): re-validates the specs, checks each library file's sha256 before decoding, renders, encodes `-c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 -ac 1` with `-fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact -map_metadata -1`, decodes the Ogg back and measures it; if the encoder pushed the true peak above -1 dBTP it re-renders with a lower ceiling (max 2 more passes, still deterministic).
- **Render host** (`host.ts`): `sshRenderHost()` ships the bundle once as `runner-<sha16>.cjs` into `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/sound-render/` and runs `flock -E 75 -w 90 render.lock timeout -k 5 120 nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 node --max-old-space-size=768 ...` with the job on stdin (one render at a time; exit 75 = busy). Injectable (tests use a fake). `selectRenderHost(env)`: OFF unless `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` (+ optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`). Audio is never rendered on the primary.
- **Determinism**: same SoundSpec + same library -> byte-identical Ogg. Verified: two real renders of the 11-file banshee set gave identical Ogg and PCM sha256 for every file, and three separate real runs built the same 1.21.11 pack (sha1 `{f1['pack']['sha1']}`). The PCM sha256 (16-bit) is recorded too, as the reference if a future ffmpeg/libvorbis changes the encoder bytes. Goldens: synth presets + the example spec are pinned by PCM hash (computed under Node 24 on node-2).

### 3. Synth presets (`synth.ts`, params in `synth-params.ts`)
Seeded (xorshift32) and pure: `growl` (jittered saw through formant band-passes), `wail` (FM sine glide, vibrato, breath), `whoosh` (noise through a swelling band-pass), `impact` (pitch-dropping thump + noise crack), `gunshot` (crack + boom + tail + slap-back), `click`, `confirm` (two-note blip; no randomness), `magic` (gliding triad, tremolo, sparkle grains). The R1 sound slice is built and committed on `feature/cyrus-r1` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r1`, 7 commits ending `28664fb1b6`). tsc is clean, the Cyrus + modbuilder suite passes 847/847, the throwaway-DB test passes 4/4, and both node-2 flights passed. Nothing is deployed or switched on, and no audio is in git.

**Biggest finding: the library has a third-party licence.** The owner's zip contains `_Essential Sound Effects Bundle License.pdf` (licensor Excelerator.tech, non-transferable). It allows modifying the sounds and using them in games. It forbids distributing the files, or making them available, alone or inside any other bundle or package. A resource pack puts the Ogg files on every player's machine. So customer builds get synth sounds only until `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` is set, and a library sound can never ship unchanged. The ledger stays exactly as you specified ("owner-provided (2026-10-10)", "unverified: owner to document source per file group").

**What was built** (all under `lib/cyrus/sound/` unless noted):
- **Library:** metadata-only manifest of the 514 MP3s, a taxonomy kept as data in `taxonomy.json`, and a search with synonyms, filters, facets and a "similar to" helper. Result: 0 files in Other and 34 with an explicit "no use case" reason (mostly music beds). I added two categories you didn't list, Music & Stingers and Magic & Energy; without them about 85 files would have landed in Other. The review report for the owner is `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/sound-library-catalog.md`.
- **Audio pipeline:** pure DSP, loudness/true-peak measurement and quality bar, 8 seeded synth presets, SoundSpec v1. The renderer runs on node-2 only, through a swappable ssh "render host".
- **Build service:** the sound prompt section (synth-only or with the read-only library catalog), sound spec checks with bounded repairs, `assetResult.sounds`. The service's validator is generated from the TS one so they cannot drift.
- **Portal:** the sound flag is on with the plan gate unchanged. Sync renders on the render host, checks each Ogg, puts `sounds.json` plus subtitles into the same pack as the textures, and records one sound asset per set. The NxLabs page says "Includes N custom sounds (subtitled); players accept a resource pack on join."

**ffmpeg:** BtbN static build `n8.1.3-16-ge0a878dd70`, `lgpl-8.1` variant, checksum verified, isolated under `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/ffmpeg`. It is LGPL v3 (`--enable-version3`, no `--enable-gpl`, no nonfree) and includes libvorbis. It only runs as a separate process.

**Determinism:** yes, byte-identical. Two real renders of the 11-file banshee set gave the same Ogg and PCM hashes for every file. Three separate runs built the same 1.21.11 pack.

**Ran on node-2:**
- **Render:** banshee set (ambient, hurt, death, attack, step) from library and synth layers. ffprobe shows every file is vorbis, 44.1 kHz, mono; all passed the quality checks.
- **Flight, Paper 1.21.11:** passed 6/6.
- **Flight, Paper 26.2:** passed 6/6 using a preview-only pack that production refuses.
- **26.2 spawn failure:** 26.2 refuses to spawn a monster in Peaceful difficulty; the prompt now tells mods to check difficulty first.

**Not run:** no real Minecraft client connected, so actual playback, subtitles and the pack prompt are not verified. No real model build was run.

**Decisions the plan didn't specify:** one spec file is a sound set with its events inside (key `<ns>:<set>.<event>`). Rendering happens at sync time, not in the build service.

**Owner must:**
1. Decide on the bundle licence and document sources per file group.
2. Review the catalog report.
3. Choose and set up the production render path (ssh key to node-2, `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`), ideally from the worker only.
4. Rebuild the build-service image with the new sound files.
5. Do a real-client listening test.

**Studio interface:** `searchLibrary`, `similarTo`, `librarySound`, `checkSoundSpec`, `SYNTH_PARAMS`, `selectRenderHost().host.render(renderJobFor(...))`, and `syncBuildAssets` producing `MbAssets.sounds`. Details are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md, section "Cyrus sound slice (R1)".
